task.title: Page complete one-shot schedule histories through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/1009 by exposing bounded schedule-history pages as deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate a positive at-most-1024 page size and optional exact schedule-ID cursor before storage access.
Emit exact-ID-ordered complete revision-bearing histories and the kernel-owned nullable exclusive continuation cursor.
Preserve missing-storage non-creation and fail without partial stdout on selected or lookahead corruption.

attempts.diagnostic: The CLI rejected schedule histories because the subcommand did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added integration tests for complete lifecycle JSON, ordering, escaping, continuation, empty and terminal pages, validation, missing storage, and corruption boundaries.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the read-only adapter.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented pre-storage validation, one read-only histories_page delegation, compact deterministic JSON, and shared exact/paged history-entry conversion.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 1009 in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs with CLI tests, ADR-0102, and scheduler documentation; independent pre-commit review found no blocking issue.

attempts.diagnostic: A review-limit false green was excluded; after cooldown, CodeRabbit run 7162704e-9e39-4754-9f47-1f1ea5fcbb53 reviewed exact head 956bbed with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled until the exact-head Rust gate and deliberate genuine review succeeded.

outcome.summary: Issue 1009 exposed bounded complete schedule-history pages without creating storage or adding write authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 1010 exact head 956bbed5504a2a294050cd261dd03e1fc660fa47

lessons: The CLI should delegate paging and corruption policy once rather than compose inventory pages with per-result exact history calls.
Sharing typed history-entry conversion keeps exact and paged commands aligned and fails closed on future unsupported event variants.
The page size bounds schedule histories, not events inside each complete lifecycle.
The adapter creates no storage, persists no cursor, reads no clock, and adds no lifecycle, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.
